thread:
Maria: Quick RFC follow-up — proposal to split 'probe' (fast, binary/compat checks) from 'bench' (full perf + quality). Move ABI/compat tests to probe so we fail fast and avoid wasting bench GPU time. Thoughts?

Ken: Agree on fail-fast, but worried about false positives for quantized builds (we'll reject a model that actually works). Need good heuristics.

Alex: We can do a layered probe: cheap static digest + tiny runtime smoke. Static digest example: sha256 of op-list + param-dtypes + kv-schema. If digest mismatches known-good families, run 1-2-step runtime smoke.

Tim: How will this surface to model owners? We should return clear 'why rejected' codes. Too many opaque rejects = tickets.

Maria: yes — standardize rejection reasons: ABI_MISMATCH, KERNEL_MISSING, QUANT_WARNT, SMOKE_FAIL. Include minimal repro artifacts (the single short trace + failing op id).

Jun: For runtime quirks I suggest an explicit 'runtime-features' handshake returned by Dedicated/Private runtimes. Probe asks /runtime/compat and gets JSON features like: {"kv_cache_v":"v2","fused_matmul":"ok","quant_4bit":"partial"} — probe uses that to decide fastpath vs slowpath.

Eve: tiny nit — probing the runtime adds network roundtrips. We should only call runtime probe when static digest is uncertain. Otherwise static rules suffice and we save latency/cost.

Alex: Agreed. Rough probe flow I sketched:

```
# pseudo-config for probe gating
probe:
  static_digest: true
  runtime_smoke_threshold: 0.2  # fraction of ambiguous digests we escalate
  smoke_steps: 2
  smoke_max_tokens: 8
  rejection_codes: [ABI_MISMATCH, KERNEL_MISSING, SMOKE_FAIL, QUANT_WARNT]
```

Ken: How do we keep bench signal quality if we accept models with fallback slowpath enabled? We might mask regressions by runtime fallbacks.

Maria: Bench stays the truth. Probe is purely admission. If probe allows a model with slowpath, bench will still run and flag regressions — but we won't block deployment on bench queue backlog.

Tim: Rollout plan idea — accept into 'fastpath off' QA tier first (no production routing), run bench + golden-eval. If quality passes, flip a canary that enables fastpath.

Jun: Need metrics instrumentation: probe.accept_rate, probe.escalation_rate, probe.reject_reason_distribution, bench.regressions_post_admit. Also tag by model-family and quant-mode.

Eve: Operational concern: KV cache mismatch (schema changes) is a common root cause. We should include a schema-version fingerprint in digest and run a small cache-warm smoke that exercises prefix reads/writes.

Maria: Good. Also propose a 'compat-ack' registry maintained by runtime/team owners (small YAML entries) so the probe can short-circuit to that when exact model family is common.

Alex: Example compat-ack entry:

```
# runtime compat registry snippet (human-editable)
- model_family: llama-3x
  supported_quant: [int8, fp16]
  known_kernel_quirks: [fused_conv_transpose]
  compat_stamp: "2026-03-10T12:00Z"
```

Ken: How do we handle externally contributed converters that change op ordering? We need a fingerprint invariant that tolerates reorderings where semantics unchanged. That's tricky.

Maria: maybe use op-multiset + param-shape-signature rather than linear op-list for digest. It's weaker but less brittle. We accept more ambiguity and escalate to smoke if the multiset classification is ambiguous.

Tim: Can we run a 'microbench' that measures a cheap kernel exec latency (single matmul) to detect pathological kernel fallback (e.g., blocked GEMM path)? That might catch perf regressions early.

Jun: Yes, 1-2 microbench ops per probe — cheap but very informative. We should cap tokens and keep it under 50ms.

Eve: Cost model: probe should be <1% of bench cost for a typical intake. We'll need quotas and a budget cap per day. Also provide a dry-run mode for model authors (simulate probe locally).

Maria: Action items I captured: 
- Alex: prototype static_digest + multiset fingerprint (P0)
- Jun: define runtime /compat API and feature schema (P0)
- Tim: rejection code taxonomy + user-facing messages (P1)
- Ken/Eve: microbench recipe + cost guardrails (P1)
- Maria: write short RFC update with rollout plan and metrics (P0)

Ken: +1, will help with microbench numbers.

Alex: I'll drop a small prototype repo link in a follow-up.

sre-bot: Deploy check — created ticket INF-2248 to track probe split rollout, assigned to Maria + Jun. :white_check_mark:

Maria: Thanks — I'll draft the RFC patch and ping runtime owners for compat-ack onboarding. :thumbsup:

Ken: quick question — can probe produce an automated follow-up issue when it rejects a model with reproducible trace? That would help scale triage.

Maria: yes — plan is to auto-create a triage issue with the probe log and failing op id, but only when owner contact is present to avoid spamming.

Eve: minor UX: include 'why-to-fix' hints in the triage issue like "try converting with converter-x --fuse-matmul=false" when possible.

Maria: Great. I'll incorporate hints list into the RFC. Closing loop — will post RFC link asap.

Alex: thanks all.
